must_catch.item: The decision-maker contradiction (Raj vs. Angela) is surfaced.
"that's a diagram" is tied to a messaging change.
The question shift (11 of 14 about stores) is reported as a fact.
The rep's "better product online" is treated as opinion, not used as a reason.

fails: Language section attributes "one customer, one basket" to Angela, COO. The transcript does not clearly say who said it, so this is a definite speaker attribution the transcript doesn't support.
data.notes: The report's biggest strength is the decider analysis. It clearly surfaces the Raj-vs-Angela contradiction: we sold to the CTO and won the web side, while the COO, who owned the store problem, signed with Adyen. It also turns 'that's a diagram' into a live till-return messaging change backed by rollout and reference proof. It misses three things. It leaves the incumbent blank (separate store and online providers) and labels the Angela December 27 story as opinion instead of secondhand fact. Its close never names the key's open questions (Adyen's commercial terms, what Bev wrote down, whether a partner-install rollout plan would have been accepted) or the follow-up to get the 14-question list from Raj. It also never explicitly flags 'better product online' as the rep's opinion; it simply leaves it out.
